chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn Qar'ah, from Zayd ibn Jaham, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The performer of Tamattu' could not find a sacrificial animal.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Did he not have one Dirham to go to his people with, so he could be saying to them, 'Participate me with this Dirham?'

key_terms.أَشْرِكُونِي: Participate with me / Join me in partnership
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A silver coin, used here as a unit of currency for pooling funds
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, combining both with a single Ihram
key_terms.هَدْياً: Sacrificial animal offered by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they cannot afford a sacrificial animal for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism for a pilgrim performing Tamattu' who lacks the funds for an individual sacrifice, permitting the pooling of resources. By contributing a single Dirham and inviting others to join, the pilgrim can collectively fulfill the hady obligation, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of shared liability in ritual duties when individual capacity is limited. This highlights the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding communal worship obligations.
